title: Micro eval surge — weekly capture and failure-mode triage
content:
Weekly capture for the sudden uptick in small-batch eval failures and related model onboarding observations (April 10–14, 2026)

Summary:
- This week focused on triaging a cluster of evaluation failures that appeared after we rolled forward the 8-bit quant profile for `rw-llama-13b` on the staging branch. Failures are concentrated on short-context QA evals and streaming chat integration tests.
- Hypothesis set: interaction between quant rounding & KV-cache population timing, slightly different sampling in the runtime kernels for short sequences, and a specific tokenizer edge-case on recently-added instruction-tuning data.
- Early revert (partial) reduced failure rate from ~7.2% -> 1.1% on staging evals; still investigating root cause.

Standup notes (by day):
- 2026-04-10 (Fri)
  - Ethan: noticed new spike in rerank/QA eval flakiness after nightly deploy. Collected failing examples (+30). Opened REDW-2741.
  - Priya: ran binary search over quantization config; failure correlated with asymmetric rounding enabled.
  - Action: snapshot model + tokenizer and pin for forensic runs.

- 2026-04-12 (Mon)
  - Luca: reproduced failure locally with minimal harness (batch_size=1, seq_len<=64). Confirmed KV cache warm-start can sometimes yield off-by-one token in cached prefixes when using continuous-batching.
  - Aisha: triggered canary that soft-falls back to float16 kernel when encountering suspicious token IDs; observed 0 failures in ~2k requests.
  - Noah: started corpus-level diff between failing & passing prompts — many failing ones contain repeated punctuation or emoji sequences.

- 2026-04-13 (Tue)
  - Team pooled to triage: prioritized three reproducible repros.
  - Quick experiment: disable asymmetric rounding + KV-cache prefetch delay of 1 step -> failure rate dropped but latency increased ~3–5ms.
  - Decided to keep partial revert on staging and run expanded regression suite overnight with more seeds.

Key observations and hypotheses (priority order):
1) Quant rounding + small-seq behavior: asymmetric rounding introduced tiny distributional shifts for logits in tail positions that propagate in low-temp sampling (seen in greedy/beam as well).
2) KV-cache population race: continuous batching can occasionally map a prefix to the wrong cache index if the prefetch/eviction timing aligns poorly with quantized layer outputs. Hard to trigger on single-GPU dev setups.
3) Tokenizer anomaly: a subset of tokens from new instruction-tuning data (special replacement chars) produce different internal token ID shapes after the tokenization sanitization pass; this interacts poorly with our sparse attention masks in the runtime.
4) Eval harness sensitivity: current short-context QA harness is sensitive to random seed & caller-supplied top_p; small sampling differences expose regressions that wouldn't appear in deterministic generation.

Experiments run this week (summary):
- Binary-searched quant parameters across 8 profiles (asymmetric rounding, calibration-bias, clip threshold). Results: asymmetric rounding = highest correlated factor with failures (p < 0.01 on sample).
- KV-cache stress harness with micro-batching (bs 1..8): reproduced 2/3 repros when continuous-batch pipeline enabled.
- Tokenizer normalization check: reran tokenization on entire failing corpus; 12 prompts showed diff from canonical tokenization used in training.
- Canary fallback test: runtime fallback to fp16 at inference-time when a token ID > 250K encountered. No failures across 2k calls.

Action items (owners + due):
- Ethan: assemble minimal reproduction scripts and curate 25 top failing prompts for the eval team (due 2026-04-16).
- Priya: implement conservative quant patch (disable asymmetric rounding) and run nightly regression across full eval suite (due 2026-04-15).
- Luca: instrument KV-cache mapping to log candidate index mismatches with trace sampling (add sampling flag) (due 2026-04-18).
- Noah: generate tokenizer diffs and propose sanitize pass change; add unit tests for the 12 problematic tokens (due 2026-04-17).
- Aisha: coordinate with release-engineering to plan a controlled progressive rollout to Dedicated with a metric gate on eval-failure-rate (goal: <0.5%) (due 2026-04-20).

Short-term mitigations applied:
- Partial revert of asymmetric rounding on staging (hotfix) — lowered failure rate but not zeroed.
- Canary fallback to fp16 on tokens outside trained vocab range for streaming chat.
- Increased eval harness sampling seeds (from 3 -> 10) to reduce false negatives during CI.

Open risks / unknowns:
- Latency cost of fallback + added prefetch delay may regress SLO at 95th percentile for small inference instances. Need to quantify impact on cost per token.
- If tokenizer sanitization fix changes token IDs for training data, we must coordinate an offline remap or accept a small drift in outputs — this has downstream eval consequences.
- Some regression patterns only show in distributed (multi-GPU) micro-batch scenarios — our local reproducibility is limited.

Longer-term notes / next research items:
- Work with research quant team to revisit calibration dataset (increase short-doc examples) and evaluate symmetric rounding with bias-correction.
- Add explicit KV-cache self-check in runtime (cheap checksum per prefix) to detect mapping mismatches early.
- Expand short-context harness to include edge-case token patterns (emoji, multi-byte punct, zero-width chars).
- Create a dedicated onboarding checklist entry to run the short-context-sensitivity suite before promoting quant profiles to staging.

Meeting artifacts and references:
- REDW-2741 (regression triage ticket)
- GH PR: quant-tests/pull/117 (adds asymmetric-rounding toggles to local harness)
- Confluence: Model Onboarding Checklist v2 (section: short-context QA)

Notes to self / friction reminders:
- Keep the failing prompt set minimal and reproducible — it makes postmortems much easier.
- We need a better convention for kernel-level toggles (env vs config) — toggles scattered across runtime make rollbacks error-prone.
- When drafting rollout policies, include cost guardrails (expected p95 latency delta and RMSE of top-k predictions).

Next sync: Thursday deep-dive (2026-04-15 09:30 PT) — bring reproduction scripts, KV-cache instrumented traces, and tokenizer diffs.

-- end of capture (Aisha)
